subtype: Lip biting when unsure or anxious [Regulating]
passage: In the changing room after training, Mateo kept biting his lower lip. The coach had put him in defence for the semi-final, and he badly wanted the striker spot back, but he didn't want to sound like he was complaining. Fatima, tying her boots, noticed the lip. "You've got that lip thing again. Something you want to say?" Mateo let go and rubbed his mouth. "I don't know. Maybe. I want to ask the coach, but I'm afraid of sounding selfish." Fatima shrugged gently. "Asking isn't selfish. I can come with you if you like." He nodded slowly, a tiny weight coming off his chest.

qa.a: The coach had put him in defence.

qa.q: What could Mateo try before speaking to the coach?
qa.a: He could plan a few calm words about what he'd like and why, and take Fatima up on coming along. A short, honest request is easier than swallowing it.

qa.q: How does Fatima see his lip biting?
qa.a: She sees it as a sign there's something he wants to say, so she asks gently. Noticing without pushing let him decide to talk.

grounding: A teenager bites his lip to hold back words while nervous, and a friend's gentle question opens it up.

Hey Divyansh,
I wanted to say thanks for yesterday.
When Coach read out the team for the tournament and my name wasn't on it, I bit my lip so hard it hurt. I didn't trust myself to say anything, because I knew it would come out angry, and Coach was already stressed.
I didn't think anyone noticed. But at the water cooler you just said, "You okay? You were biting your lip." You didn't push, and when I shrugged, you only said, "If you want to rant later, I'm around."
Last night I did rant, for an hour. Sorry about that.
It helped. Today I asked Coach calmly what I need to work on.
Yash

"Omkar, you asked why I was so quiet at dinner last Sunday. Okay.
My uncle started saying that art is a waste of time, and that kids who draw won't get jobs. And he was looking right at me, because everyone knows I want to do design.
I wanted to argue so badly. But it was a family dinner, and Papa gave me a look. So I bit my lip. Really hard. I kept biting it through the whole dessert.

That text made me feel less alone. I'm still going to talk to my uncle. Just not in front of twenty people. I'm Nilesh, not a fighter at dinner parties."

subtype: Lip biting when unsure or anxious [Regulating]
passage:
Before our science viva, Manjula sat next to me outside the lab, waiting for her name. She was biting her bottom lip, first one side, then the other. Her knee bounced.
I couldn't tell if she was nervous or just thinking hard about the questions. Manjula is usually the calm one.
I asked quietly, "Nervous?"
She let go of her lip. "A bit. I forgot the formula for density this morning."
"Mass over volume," I said.
She repeated it twice, then smiled. "Thanks."
When her name was called, she walked in without biting her lip. Later she told me the examiner asked about density first.
- Jomon

qa.q: What formula had Manjula forgotten?
qa.a: The formula for density.

qa.q: What might Manjula have been feeling while biting her lip?
qa.a: She was probably anxious about the viva, though Jomon couldn't be sure if she was nervous or thinking hard.

qa.q: What did Jomon do that helped?
qa.a: Jomon noticed the lip biting and asked one gentle question, which let Manjula share her worry and get quick help.

qa.q: What would change if Jomon had said nothing?
qa.a: Manjula might have walked in still anxious and without the density formula, which turned out to be the examiner's first question.

grounding: An observer notices a classmate biting her lip before a viva and opens a gentle question.
